boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Ball's Bluff record (October 21, 1861) in McClellan's Operations in Northern Virginia [October-December 1861]. McCall's move to Dranesville, the October 20 demonstration at Edwards Ferry and the October 22 action near Edwards Ferry are context. Campaign-wide movements, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen and live force fields read 3,600 (US 2,000; CS 1,600). Stone says Baker had between 1,600 and 1,700 bayonets on the field, that the enemy was nearly if not quite three to one, that he had warned Baker of about 4,000 opposed, and that reports of 10,000 were highly exaggerated. Evans gives his own force as 1,709 aggregate, and the enemy's as five regiments and three guns at Ball's Bluff and about 8,000 in all, including the Edwards Ferry force.
claims.rationale: Figures differ in scope (field at the bluff, the whole crossing, each side's estimate of the other). None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.rationale: Ground from the two commanders and a summary; no map inspected.

claims.value: Stone's memoranda give Baker boats for 172 men at 6 a.m., raised to 272 with a canal boat, and argue that managed in order they could have crossed 720 to 1,080 men an hour; his report says no system was enforced at the landings, artillery was sent before its infantry, and the largest boat swamped in the retreat. Evans says his troops fought without food or rest for more than twelve hours before the battle.
claims.rationale: Stone's figures are his own post-battle memoranda written under criticism; no quartermaster return inspected.

claims.value: The frozen and live commanders are Brigadier General Nathan Evans and Brigadier General Charles P. Stone, and the frozen list adds Colonel Edward Baker. Stone says he gave Baker entire control on the right with discretion to withdraw or cross, and in his November 2 letter blames Baker for determining to bring on an action, mishandling the crossing and posting; he says Baker replied 'I shall not retire.' Baker was killed about 4 p.m. Evans directed his regiments into the fight, says Jenifer commanded only the first five companies, and says Stone was superseded by Banks at 3 a.m. on the 22nd.
claims.rationale: Stone's attribution of fault to Baker is an interested account written under newspaper attack; Baker left no report in the inspected pages. No listed commander receives automatic sole credit or blame.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory. Evans says his charge drove the enemy into the river and that the force at Ball's Bluff surrendered at 8 p.m.; Stone says the troops fought at the bluff until the boats were gone and then swam, surrendered or hid; NPS calls it a Union rout. NPS's statement that the rout led to the Joint Committee on the Conduct of the War is political contribution, not tactical outcome.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty fields read 1,070 (US 921; CS 149); NPS says more than 700 Federals were captured and Baker killed. Evans puts the enemy's loss at 1,300 killed, wounded and drowned, with 710 prisoners, three guns and 1,500 stand of arms taken; his own loss statement is omitted from the printed report and referred to a separate return.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Evans's report covers October 21-22; the Edwards Ferry action is not added to the Ball's Bluff record.

open_questions: The Union casualty return (No. 3, total 921 as printed) and the Confederate return (No. 22) were read but not selected; McClellan's report, the regimental reports (Devens, Hinks, Palfrey, Cogswell, Wistar and others), Buxton's strength report, and Barksdale's, Featherston's, Hunton's, Jenifer's and the other Confederate reports remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Stone's October 29 report, November 2 letter and November 6 memoranda (Official Records Series I, Volume V) are one family of interested Union accounts, written in part to answer newspaper criticism. Evans's October 31, 1861 report and March 7, 1862 letter (same volume) are one family of interested Confederate accounts. The Official Records volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge. No Scribner Campaigns of the Civil War volume narrating this engagement was inspected; Nicolay's volume ends in July 1861.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
